What Really Happened at BioSource

Leia o texto uma vez. Depois, para cada suposição abaixo, monte a pergunta certa (na estrutura indicada) antes de conferir se o texto confirma ou desmente. Use a lupa se precisar reler o trecho exato.

The Full Story

Mariana Voss has spent the past two weeks trying to put BioSource back on solid ground. The shipment from VanderChem was supposed to arrive on a Monday, three weeks ago, and it still hasn't shown up. She has already contacted four potential backup suppliers in Rotterdam and São Paulo. According to the original contract, VanderChem must notify BioSource 30 days before any price change. They never did. Mariana thinks the company should have activated a backup supplier the moment the first delay happened, not three weeks later.

Rafael Moura, the Procurement Director at Frigorex, has called BioSource twice this week alone. He wants to know whether the enzyme shipment is still on schedule. Mariana has told him the truth: the delay is real, and a partial batch is the only realistic solution for now. Frigorex's own contract states that a supplier must give at least 48 hours' notice before any change to a confirmed delivery date. BioSource gave less than 24.

Lars, the account manager at VanderChem, has finally admitted that the delay was caused by a shortage of raw materials. He says the company should have flagged the shortage before confirming the shipment date, not after. VanderChem is supposed to hold a valid export license for every batch it ships internationally. That license, it turns out, expired two weeks before the shipment was due. Mariana has asked her legal team to review every clause in the VanderChem contract line by line.

The backup supplier in Rotterdam, a company called Halvorsen Ingredients, has already sent samples for testing. According to their onboarding checklist, a new supplier is supposed to complete a full quality audit before the first order is approved. Mariana thinks the team should double-check Halvorsen's certifications one more time before signing anything. A supplier declaring force majeure must provide documented proof of the event, and Halvorsen has already done exactly that for a separate, unrelated delay last year. That track record has reassured Mariana more than any sales pitch could.

David, the new analyst on Mariana's team, has already drafted three different templates for supplier warning letters. Mariana believes every analyst should learn to write one of these letters within the first month on the job. The standard notice period in most long-term supply contracts is supposed to give both sides at least 90 days' warning before either can exit. VanderChem's contract, oddly, was signed with only a 30-day notice period. Mariana must decide by Friday whether to renew that contract or let it expire.

The team has already prepared a full report comparing VanderChem's and Halvorsen's pricing, delivery times, and certifications. Mariana thinks the board should see that report before any final decision is made. Frigorex is supposed to receive a written apology and a revised delivery schedule by the end of the week. A distributor must request written approval before reselling the enzyme to a third country, and VanderChem has never once asked for that approval from BioSource. Mariana has learned, if nothing else, that a contract is only as strong as the trust behind it.

Quick Help · Ajuda Rápida
How to form the question
Como montar a pergunta

Invert the subject and the auxiliary/modal verb — put it first.
Inverta o sujeito e o verbo auxiliar/modal, colocando-o primeiro.

Claim: "The shipment was supposed to arrive on Monday." ↓ invert Question: "Was the shipment supposed to arrive on Monday?"
Must → have to (in questions)
Com "must", a pergunta usa "have to"

English doesn't invert "must" to ask a question — use "does/do ... have to" instead.
Não invertemos "must" para perguntar — usamos "does/do ... have to".

Claim: "VanderChem must give 30 days' notice." ↓ Question: "Does VanderChem have to give 30 days' notice?"
Should vs. Should have
A diferença entre os dois
should + verb Opinion about now or the future
Opinião sobre o presente/futuro
"The team should double-check the certifications."
should have + participle Criticism about the past — something that didn't happen
Crítica sobre o passado — algo que não aconteceu
"VanderChem should have flagged the shortage."
